normal.notes:
Much less data, in every quality setting. Data Saver now really saves data: it streams a smaller picture at a lower frame rate, so an hour of normal desktop work uses a fraction of what it did. Balanced, Sharp and High are also lighter, because this Mac no longer resends a full-screen picture every two seconds and sends almost nothing while the screen isn't changing.

Nothing streams when nobody is watching. When your iPhone goes to the background or the viewer window is hidden, this Mac stops sending the picture straight away and picks up again the moment you come back. A session left paused over the internet for an hour is closed for you. Sessions on the same network are never cut.

Smoother on slow connections: on a weak link the picture now steps down in quality instead of stalling.

beta.notes:
Quality: every session starts at Data Saver; the auth IDR waits up to 700 ms for .setQuality so the first keyframe is already at the viewer's size. Long-edge caps DS 1280 / Smooth+Balanced 1920 / Sharp 2880 / High 3840. Per-mode send gate (DS ~180 KB vs fixed 512 KB) + congestion controller (drop-IDR spacing 0.5->2 s, bitrate x0.7 steps, floor 40%, +5%/s recovery, never above the mode cap). VT property failures logged per key; DataRateLimits falls back to a 1 s window. Drop-IDR retry until the send gate has its keyframe.

Idle: encoding stops while the viewer is paused; internet-only deadlines: paused 60 min (4 h with audio), legacy viewers without the capability byte 4 h with no input. Same-network sessions exempt. Host window polls the Pro badge at most every 5 min; data meter polls only during a live session.
